Definition: from G3326 and G2983; to participate; genitive case, to accept (and use):--eat, have, be partaker, receive, take.
BiblicalUsage: This word covers both taking and sharing: the earth receives blessing when it drinks in the rain, the believer is made a partaker of God's holiness, and Paul urges hungry sailors to take food after fourteen days without eating. Receiving and participating turn out to be the same motion.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the Christian life is mostly receiving well: the earth does not earn the rain, the child does not earn the discipline, and we do not earn holiness — we take part in what God gives. The earth drinks the rain, the child takes the discipline, and we take part in holiness — all of it received, none of it earned.
